---
title: "Cobb-Douglas: cost minimisation and factor shares"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

{{< include _sequence.qmd >}}

This page takes the [isoquants](index.qmd) of the Cobb-Douglas production
function, $q = A L^a K^b$, and asks how a firm would choose to produce a given
quantity $q$ if each unit of labour costs $w$ and each unit of capital costs $r$.

An isocost line shows all the combinations of labour and capital with the same
total cost, $C = wL + rK$. It is a straight line with slope $-w/r$, and lines
further from the origin cost more. The cheapest way to produce $q$ is the point
on its isoquant that touches the lowest possible isocost line. There the two
have the same slope, which for a Cobb-Douglas function means

$$
\frac{K}{L} = \frac{b}{a} \cdot \frac{w}{r} .
$$

So when labour becomes more expensive relative to capital, the firm uses more
capital per worker. The shares of total cost going to each input, however, do not
change: labour always receives $a / (a + b)$ of the total and capital
$b / (a + b)$, whatever the prices. With constant returns to scale these are
simply $a$ and $1 - a$. The bar under the chart shows the two shares: change $w$
or $r$ and the chosen point moves, but the split stays the same; change $a$ or
$b$ and the split moves.

::: {.sim-layout}

::: {.sim-controls}

{{< include _controls.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof q = Inputs.range([1, 10], {value: 4, step: 0.5, label: "Output to produce, q"})
viewof w = Inputs.range([0.5, 3], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "Cost of labour, w"})
viewof r = Inputs.range([0.5, 3], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "Cost of capital, r"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
best = minimiseCost(q, p, w, r)

// Both axes run from 0 to max: 10, or further if the chosen point needs it.
max = Math.max(10, 1.25 * Math.max(best.L, best.K))

isoquants = levels.flatMap(level => isoquant(level, p, max))
target = isoquant(q, p, max)

// Isocost lines at half, exactly, and one and a half times the minimum cost.
isocosts = [0.5, 1, 1.5].map(m => ({
  minimum: m === 1,
  ends: [{L: 0, K: m * best.cost / r}, {L: m * best.cost / w, K: 0}]
}))

shares = [
  {factor: "Labour", cost: best.labourCost, share: best.labourCost / best.cost},
  {factor: "Capital", cost: best.capitalCost, share: best.capitalCost / best.cost}
]

colours = ({isoquant: "#4269d0", isocost: "#ff725c", labour: "#3ca951", capital: "#efb118"})
```

$a + b =$ ${scale.toFixed(2)}: ${returns} returns to scale. ${bNote}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<p>Cheapest way to produce <em>q</em> = ${q}: <em>L</em> = ${best.L.toFixed(2)},
<em>K</em> = ${best.K.toFixed(2)}, so <em>K</em> / <em>L</em> = ${(best.K / best.L).toFixed(2)}.</p>
<p>Total cost = ${best.cost.toFixed(2)}: labour ${best.labourCost.toFixed(2)}
(${(100 * shares[0].share).toFixed(0)}%), capital ${best.capitalCost.toFixed(2)}
(${(100 * shares[1].share).toFixed(0)}%).</p>`
```

:::

::: {.sim-output}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  width: 560,
  height: 560,
  x: {label: "Labour, L", domain: [0, max], ticks: 5},
  y: {label: "Capital, K", domain: [0, max], ticks: 5},
  color: {
    legend: true,
    domain: [`isoquant, q = ${q}`, "isocost lines"],
    range: [colours.isoquant, colours.isocost]
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.line(isoquants, {x: "L", y: "K", z: "q", stroke: colours.isoquant, strokeOpacity: 0.2, clip: true}),
    // Isocost lines: the minimum-cost one solid, the others dashed.
    isocosts.map(line => Plot.line(line.ends, {
      x: "L", y: "K", stroke: () => "isocost lines", clip: true,
      strokeWidth: line.minimum ? 2 : 1, strokeDasharray: line.minimum ? null : "4,3"
    })),
    Plot.line(target, {x: "L", y: "K", stroke: () => `isoquant, q = ${q}`, strokeWidth: 2, clip: true}),
    // The cost-minimising point, with the amounts of labour and capital it uses.
    Plot.ruleX([best], {x: "L", y1: 0, y2: "K", stroke: colours.labour, strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
    Plot.ruleY([best], {y: "K", x1: 0, x2: "L", stroke: colours.capital, strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
    Plot.dot([best], {x: "L", y: "K", fill: "currentColor", r: 5}),
    Plot.text([best], {x: "L", y: "K", text: () => "lowest cost", textAnchor: "start", dx: 9, dy: -9})
  ]
})
```

**Shares of total cost**

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  width: 560,
  height: 70,
  marginLeft: 40,
  x: {label: "share of total cost, %", domain: [0, 100]},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(shares, Plot.stackX({x: d => 100 * d.share, fill: d => colours[d.factor.toLowerCase()]})),
    Plot.text(shares, Plot.stackX({
      x: d => 100 * d.share,
      text: d => `${d.factor} ${(100 * d.share).toFixed(0)}%`
    }))
  ]
})
```
